literature_notes: MS4A12 is a four-transmembrane (MS4A-family) protein with an intracellular N-terminus (residues 1–92) and an intracellular C-terminus (residues 222–267). Its only extracellular-facing regions are ECL1 (residues 114–127, 14 aa) and ECL2 (residues 184–200, 17 aa). The entire ledger (L1–L4) derives from a single paper (PMC8112172) that describes two tagged constructs: (1) GCaMP6s-MS4A12, where the cloning order (BamHI/SpeI for GCaMP6s, SpeI/XhoI for MS4A12 in pLenti6.3) places GCaMP6s N-terminal to MS4A12, i.e., on the intracellular face; and (2) 3X FLAG-MS4A12, named in the standard [tag]-[protein] convention, also placing FLAG at the intracellular N-terminus. The paper confirms that the full-length protein traffics to the plasma membrane (surface display of the protein), but neither tag is on the extracellular face. No ledger clip documents an insertion in ECL1, ECL2, or any other extracellular position. Because no qualifying extracellular insertion is grounded in the ledger, zero sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: GCaMP6s fused N-terminally to MS4A12 (cloning order: GCaMP6s BamHI/SpeI then MS4A12 SpeI/XhoI), placing the tag on the intracellular N-terminus (residues 1–92 are intracellular); protein reaches the plasma membrane but the tag faces the cytoplasm.

3X FLAG-MS4A12 sub-cloned into pCMV5; the '3X flag-MS4A12' naming convention places FLAG at the N-terminus, which is intracellular (residues 1–92); no residue number or extracellular position is stated.
